overview: Fox Corporation is a U.S. news, sports and entertainment media company formed in 2019 when 21st Century Fox spun off its news and sports assets after selling its entertainment/studio businesses to Disney. The company operates through two reportable segments — Cable Network Programming (FOX News, FOX Business, FS1/FS2, Big Ten Network) and Television (the FOX broadcast network, 29 owned-and-operated local TV stations, the Tubi AVOD streaming service, and the new FOX One direct-to-consumer subscription service). It is controlled by the Murdoch family through a dual-class share structure (FOXA non-voting/limited-voting Class A and FOX voting Class B shares).

business_model.summary: Fox generates revenue primarily from two sources: affiliate/distribution fees paid by pay-TV operators and vMVPDs for carrying its cable networks and local stations, and advertising sold across linear TV, digital (Tubi), and streaming (FOX One). Sports programming rights (NFL, MLB, Big Ten/college football, NASCAR, FIFA World Cup) are a central cost driver and audience draw across both segments. Content and other revenue (licensing, studio lot rental, Credible consumer-finance marketplace) is a smaller residual stream.

revenue_streams.name: Distribution/Affiliate fees
revenue_streams.trend: stable/low-growth as pay-TV subscribers decline but per-subscriber rates and new streaming (FOX One) distribution offset volume losses

revenue_streams.name: Advertising
revenue_streams.trend: growing, volatile - boosted by biennial sports mega-events (World Cup, Super Bowl rotation, election cycles) and secular Tubi/digital growth

business_model.customer_type: B2B (pay-TV distributors, advertisers/agencies) and B2C (Tubi and FOX One direct subscribers/viewers)
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly United States; minor international licensing and NFL Mexico broadcast rights

main_competitors: Netflix and YouTube TV/YouTube (sports streaming and ad-supported video)
competitive_position.market_position: Fox News is the dominant cable news network, holding roughly 60% of cable news viewing share and topping the category for 20+ consecutive quarters; FOX broadcast network and FOX Sports hold marquee sports rights (NFL NFC package, World Series/MLB postseason, Big Ten football, NASCAR, FIFA World Cup rotation) that make it a top-rated broadcast network during football season; Tubi is a top-3 U.S. AVOD service by engagement with 110 million monthly active users.

moat_factors.description: Marquee, hard-to-replicate live sports rights (NFL, World Series, Big Ten, NASCAR, World Cup rotation) and the #1 cable news brand generate must-have, DVR-proof, appointment viewing that underpins both affiliate and advertising pricing power
Long-term carriage agreements with pay-TV and vMVPD operators provide contracted, largely non-cyclical fee revenue, though renewal negotiations face pressure from a shrinking subscriber base
Highly loyal, ideologically distinct audience base that has proven resilient to competitive and political pressures
29 owned stations in large markets provide retransmission fees, local advertising and NFL/sports lead-in audiences
Growing AVOD and SVOD footprint (Tubi at 110M MAU, profitable; pending Roku acquisition would add first-party CTV data and 100M+ streaming households) reduces reliance on the legacy pay-TV bundle

weaknesses: No streaming/entertainment studio scale versus Disney, Netflix, WBD, or Comcast — Fox lacks a large scripted content library or film studio (sold to Disney in 2019)
Heavy dependence on a small number of very expensive sports rights contracts (NFL, MLB) that renew on the league's terms
Cable network segment exposed to structural pay-TV subscriber decline (cord-cutting) eroding the affiliate-fee base over time
Fox News' partisan positioning creates advertiser boycotts/brand-safety risk and periodic defamation/legal exposure (e.g., Dominion settlement precedent)
Smaller overall scale than mega-cap media/tech peers, limiting negotiating leverage with the NFL and complicating funding of the pending $22B Roku acquisition

growth_drivers: Tubi: record revenue (+25-35% YoY in FY2026), 110M monthly active users, now consistently EBITDA-positive, monetizing cord-cutter/cord-never audiences with digital advertising

FOX One direct-to-consumer streaming service (launched August 2025) bundling FOX Sports/News/Entertainment linear feeds; exceeded subscriber expectations in FY2026, adding subscribers mostly from outside the traditional pay-TV bundle

Pending acquisition of Roku (~$22B enterprise value, announced June 2026, expected to close H1 calendar 2027) to combine Fox content/Tubi with Roku's CTV platform, first-party data and 100M+ global streaming households — potential ad-tech and distribution flywheel

Marquee live-sports calendar: NFL (through 2029-30 season), MLB World Series/postseason (through 2028), Big Ten football (including newly added Big Ten Championship game), NASCAR (through 2031), and FIFA World Cup rotation (2026 men's tournament boosted FY2026 advertising +78% in Q4)
Fox News' sustained #1 cable-news ratings share supports affiliate-fee renewals and premium advertising rates even as linear cable erodes
NFL Mexico broadcast exclusivity starting 2027 season adds incremental international sports advertising/distribution
Disciplined capital return (buybacks, dividend) supported by strong free cash flow generation despite heavy sports-rights amortization

business.description: Structural decline in traditional cable/satellite subscribers erodes the affiliate-fee base (47% of revenue) over time even as per-subscriber rates rise

NFL has reportedly sought to roughly double/50%+ increase rights fees at future renewal; Fox has so far declined to renegotiate early (opt-out not until after 2029-30 season), deferring the cost decision but leaving a large future step-up in content costs (BofA cited this in a February 2026 downgrade)

business.risk: Concentration in a handful of marquee sports contracts
business.description: Loss of any single major rights package (NFL, MLB, Big Ten) would materially impair both advertising and affiliate revenue and audience reach

business.risk: Fox News controversy/brand-safety and legal exposure
business.description: Prior defamation litigation (Dominion Voting Systems $787.5M settlement in 2023) and ongoing scrutiny of editorial content create episodic legal, reputational and advertiser-boycott risk

The pending ~$22B Roku acquisition (largest in Fox's history) carries integration, cultural and technology risk, and its ad-tech/CTV business model differs materially from Fox's traditional media operations

financial.description: Cash-and-stock Roku deal will require new debt issuance and dilution (0.9693 FOX shares plus $96 cash per Roku share); leverage and share count will rise post-close (expected H1 CY2027)

financial.risk: Cash flow volatility around sports-rights amortization cycles
financial.description: Free cash flow swings meaningfully between odd/even fiscal halves and years depending on Super Bowl rotation, World Cup, and NFL season timing

regulatory.description: A $22B combination of a major broadcaster/content owner with the largest CTV platform in the U.S. will draw DOJ/FTC and possibly FCC scrutiny over data, advertising and platform-neutrality concerns

regulatory.risk: FCC ownership rules / retransmission consent regulation
regulatory.description: Local station ownership caps and retransmission consent rules affect station group strategy; sports-rights migration to streaming has also drawn broadcaster pressure for FCC action to preserve local carriage rules
Periodic political pressure on cable news content and potential changes to broadcast license/public-interest obligations

macro.description: Ad revenue (42% of sales) is sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, and non-election/non-World-Cup years see a step-down in ad revenue growth

macro.risk: Interest rate exposure on acquisition financing
macro.description: Higher-for-longer rates raise the cost of debt likely to be issued to help fund the Roku transaction
Revenue and advertising are naturally lumpy across the two-year political/World-Cup cycle, complicating YoY comparisons

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. TV/media industry is bifurcated: linear pay-TV continues to shrink (mid-single-digit annual subscriber declines industry-wide) while streaming/AVOD and live sports rights costs both continue to rise sharply (industry sports-rights spend up ~75% from 2021 to 2026 per Ampere estimates). Companies with must-have live content (news, sports) are best positioned to hold pricing power through the transition.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - advertising revenue is macro- and event-cycle sensitive (elections, World Cup, Super Bowl rotation); affiliate/distribution fees are contractual and more stable but structurally declining in unit volume
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - rising given planned debt financing for the Roku acquisition; otherwise low direct sensitivity given strong free cash flow generation
key_input_costs: Sports programming rights (NFL, MLB, Big Ten, NASCAR, FIFA)
Technology/streaming infrastructure (Tubi, FOX One, and post-close Roku platform)

recent_developments.event: Fox enters fiscal 2027 citing momentum from World Cup-driven Q4/Q1 results, Tubi profitability, FOX One subscriber growth (mostly from cord-cutters/cord-nevers), and new NFL Mexico broadcast exclusivity starting the 2027 season; management flagged regulatory review, sports-rights renewals and Roku integration as the key tests ahead

Reported Q4/FY2026 results: Q4 revenue of $4.21B (+28% YoY) driven by the FIFA World Cup and Tubi; FY2026 revenue of $17.13B, net income of $1.73B, Adjusted EBITDA of $3.91B; Tubi delivered its highest-revenue quarter ever with Q4 revenue growth of 35%; adjusted EPS of $1.79 beat consensus by over 33%

CEO Lachlan Murdoch announced Fox will not renegotiate its NFL media rights early, declining the league's push to raise fees now in exchange for removing Fox's opt-out option before the deal's 2029-30 expiration

Fox Corporation announced a definitive agreement to acquire Roku, Inc. for ~$22B enterprise value ($96 cash + 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per Roku share, ~$160/share), combining Fox content/Tubi with Roku's CTV platform and 100M+ streaming households; expected to close H1 calendar 2027, pending regulatory and shareholder approval
Bank of America downgraded Fox from Buy to Underperform, cutting its price target from $80 to $45, citing concerns over looming NFL contract renewal costs

Fox officially launched FOX One, its direct-to-consumer subscription streaming service (linear sports/news/entertainment bundle) priced at $19.99/month or $199.99/year, targeting cord-cutters and cord-nevers ahead of the college football and NFL seasons
Tubi reported profitability (EBITDA-positive) for the first time on a full-quarter basis, with revenue up 27% YoY
Fox News maintained roughly 60% share of cable news viewing and topped the cable news category for 20+ consecutive quarters, continuing to outdraw CNN and MS NOW combined

items.target: step-down expected vs. FY2026 World Cup-boosted comparison, offset partly by continued Tubi/digital growth
items.notes: Management has not issued formal point-estimate revenue/EPS guidance (Fox does not provide detailed forward numerical guidance); qualitative commentary emphasizes continued Tubi growth, FOX One subscriber ramp, and NFL Mexico rights starting 2027 season as offsets to the loss of World Cup timing benefit

items.target: no new deal until closer to 2029-30 season expiration
items.notes: CEO Lachlan Murdoch stated Fox will not amend its existing NFL contract early despite league pressure, deferring a potentially large step-up in rights costs

items.target: expected to close in H1 calendar 2027
items.notes: Subject to Roku shareholder approval and regulatory clearance (S-4 registration statement filed); deal terms $96 cash + 0.9693 FOX shares per Roku share (~$160/share, ~$22B enterprise value)

items.target: continued double-digit revenue growth and sustained EBITDA profitability
items.notes: Tubi was EBITDA-positive every quarter of FY2026 with record 110M MAU and 13.2B hours viewed (+20% YoY); management expects momentum to continue

guidance.management_commentary: President and COO John Nallen described Fox as entering fiscal 2027 'exceptionally well positioned to drive sustained growth and long-term shareholder value,' citing strong momentum across the portfolio, but flagged regulatory review of the Roku deal, sports-rights renewal dynamics, and integration work as the key items to watch. Fox does not provide formal quantitative revenue/EPS guidance, consistent with historical practice.

bull_case: Fox News' dominant, durable cable-news audience share (~60%) and marquee live-sports rights (NFL, MLB, Big Ten, NASCAR, World Cup rotation) provide pricing power and advertiser demand that are difficult for competitors to replicate
Tubi has scaled to 110M monthly active users and turned sustainably EBITDA-positive, giving Fox a genuine, profitable foothold in ad-supported streaming without cannibalizing linear economics
The pending Roku acquisition could create a powerful combined CTV/content/data platform, diversifying Fox beyond legacy pay-TV distribution and unlocking ad-tech synergies

By declining to renegotiate NFL rights early, management avoided locking in a large near-term cost step-up, preserving optionality and free cash flow through the remainder of the current contract (into the 2029-30 season)

Strong free cash flow generation and shareholder-friendly capital allocation (buybacks, dividends) at a valuation (mid-teens trailing P/E, ~10x forward P/E per FY2025/26 metrics) that looks inexpensive relative to media/tech peers
bear_case: Structural cord-cutting continues to shrink the traditional pay-TV affiliate-fee base, Fox's largest revenue stream, with no guarantee FOX One/streaming distribution fully offsets the decline

NFL rights costs are widely expected to rise sharply (up to +50-100%) whenever Fox does eventually renew, which BofA specifically flagged in its February 2026 downgrade to Underperform; deferring the decision does not eliminate the eventual cash-flow hit

The ~$22B Roku acquisition is a large, complex, dilutive (cash + stock) deal carrying integration risk, incremental leverage, and regulatory/antitrust uncertainty, with closing not expected until H1 calendar 2027

Murdoch family's dual-class control structure (~40% voting power via LGC Holdco despite far smaller economic ownership) limits public shareholders' influence over major capital allocation and M&A decisions, including the Roku deal itself

Fox News' partisan brand positioning creates recurring legal/reputational risk (e.g., the 2023 $787.5M Dominion defamation settlement) and periodic advertiser boycott risk that could pressure the cable-news advertising base
Revenue and earnings are naturally lumpy across the two-year election/World Cup/Super Bowl rotation cycle, making sustained growth harder to demonstrate in off-years
